clue.text: What shearer has to rip off?

definitions.meaning: a sheep's woolly coat, which the shearer removes in one piece

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what a sheep-shearer gets to strip off the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses meet in the pun: the shearer literally strips the wool off, while the slang verb means to cheat someone of their money.
explanation.definitionFit: The wool shorn from a sheep is its coat, and the same word is a verb for cheating someone out of money.

clue.text: Turn up if general networker?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning a word up means reading it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned
William Tecumseh Sherman was a Union general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A question about whether some general would show up to a networking event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'networker' suggests business contacts, but here it is someone who works with nets. The question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler who casts nets for a living works with nets, a punning description of someone fishing commercially.

clue.text: Sign up some sailor, never seeking promotion

indicators.note: a word going up the column in a down clue is read in reverse, as if rising in rank
only part of the following words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A recruiter enlists a sailor who has no ambition to rise in the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes LORNE from sailoR NEver; 'seeking promotion' sends it up the column, giving it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your name down as a member or recruit is to register formally.

clue.text: Cobblers whack nail

parts.note: to clap is to strike with a sharp slap
to nail someone is to catch them out, to trap them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' looks like shoemakers, but it is British slang for nonsense (from rhyming slang, cobblers' awls = balls).
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for rubbish talk, empty pretentious nonsense.

clue.text: Bob possibly takes the easy way

definitions.meaning: a bob is one example of a brief hairstyle
a quicker route or method that saves effort

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob chooses the path of least resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' reads as a man's name, but it is the hairstyle: a bob is an example of short hair, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a cropped hairstyle, and a quicker route that saves effort shares the same two-word name.

clue.text: Domestic bliss on the cards?

parts.note: contented households in prospect, but read literally it is a card game where players collect sets of family members

explanation.walkthrough: 'on the cards' looks like 'likely to happen', but it also points to the British children's card game in which you collect sets of four family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Contented households are a picture of domestic contentment, and the phrase also names a traditional children's card game.

clue.text: Article in shop

definitions.meaning: a piece of writing in a newspaper
to shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the authorities

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is only a link. 'shop' as a verb is British slang for betraying someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper piece is a written account, and informing on someone to police means telling on them.

clue.text: Hail of bullets put out with strong emotion

parts.note: someone put out is annoyed, cross
fire is passion or ardour

explanation.surface: Soldiers come under a barrage while seething with anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunfire coming from two or more directions at once, a lethal barrage.

clue.text: Dance beat given energy

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to thrash them
go means vigour or energy

explanation.surface: A dance rhythm is pepped up with extra vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A passionate Argentine ballroom step for couples.

clue.text: Bumble's law on drink claiming right to supply best

indicators.note: in an across clue the law sits on, after, the drink piece
the drink takes in the letter for right, holding it inside

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
Mr Bumble, the beadle in Dickens's Oliver Twist, declares that 'the law is a ass'

explanation.surface: A beadle's legal opinion delivered over drinks, somehow providing the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' is a verb here, to outdo, not an adjective. 'claiming' means the drink holds the right inside, and 'on' sets Bumble's donkey after it in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or outdo a rival is to go beyond them.

clue.text: Dean's rude chef sacked — no sympathy here

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out and reshuffled, as a sacked chef is sent packing

parts.note: taken with its S as part of the letter pool

explanation.surface: A rude cook fired by a man named Dean gets no sympathy from anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges all thirteen letters of DEANS RUDE CHEF. The definition fits the surface too: delight at the chef's downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The German-borrowed word for taking pleasure in another's misfortune, the opposite of feeling compassion.

clue.text: Feature accompaniment with modern music, banal stuff

parts.note: pop is popular modern music
corn is trite, sentimental material

explanation.surface: A film critic dismisses a feature's soundtrack of pop songs as trite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature accompaniment' sounds like a film score, but it is the snack eaten while watching a feature film.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffed maize snack traditionally munched in cinemas during a movie.

clue.text: Striking effect as powder keg's contents knocked over

indicators.note: the whole sequence is upset and read in reverse order

parts.note: talc is talcum powder

indicators.note: the inside of the word keg, its middle letter

explanation.surface: An explosive result when a keg of powder is tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' takes E from the middle of 'keg's'; 'knocked over' turns TALC+E backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for brilliance of success or display, a dazzling show.

clue.text: Man with battle to find tricky words?

parts.note: he stands for a male person
Ypres in Belgium was the site of several First World War battles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier fresh from battle tries to find clever things to say.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on a conjuror's 'tricky words', the phrase said as a trick is completed.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation a magician utters at the moment a trick is revealed.

clue.text: Killer has to drag off heads of all and sundry

parts.note: must means is obliged to

indicators.note: the word drag goes off, out of order, and is rearranged
the first letters of the words all and sundry

explanation.surface: A murderer is obliged to haul away everyone's heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges DRAG as ARDG; 'heads of' takes A and S from 'all' and 'sundry', with 'and' just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous chemical weapon from the First World War, deadly to those exposed.

clue.text: Dessert from America may make rats choke

indicators.note: the letters of the following words may be reworked to make something new

explanation.surface: An American pudding so dry it might cause rodents to gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' rearranges RATS CHOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet American biscuit-like cake usually served with strawberries and cream.

clue.text: Time for a chat, perhaps

definitions.meaning: doing ... is British slang for serving a prison sentence
the stonechat and whinchat are small songbirds

explanation.walkthrough: 'chat' reads as a conversation, but it is a small songbird. 'Time' is British prison slang, as in 'doing bird' (from rhyming slang bird-lime = time).
explanation.definitionFit: Prison slang for a jail sentence, and also the class of feathered creatures a stonechat belongs to.

clue.text: Stop man getting cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to prevent or discourage
gent is short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A man who becomes a cleaner is told to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A washing agent such as soap powder used for laundry or dishes.

clue.text: Rush to make breakfast, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to ... eggs is one way to cook a morning meal

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to cook the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurried scrimmage, and the verb for whisking eggs as they cook in a pan.

clue.text: Twelve — no cricket side!

parts.note: taken as written
the on side is the leg side of the field in cricket

explanation.surface: A team short of its full twelve is no side at all.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock in the daytime.

clue.text: Tactless, as one is overheard

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than read, a soundalike

parts.note: indiscrete means not divided into separate parts, so united

explanation.surface: Someone is careless in speech while listeners eavesdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. The soundalike, spelt with -ETE, is a rare word meaning undivided.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless about what one says or reveals, lacking discretion.

clue.text: Class comprising a load of drips?

definitions.meaning: a school group of pupils sorted by ability
many drops of water together form a flowing brook

explanation.surface: A class full of feeble pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drips' reads as wimps, but here it means drops of water; British schools sort pupils by ability into sets of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A school ability group, and a small river made of countless drops of water.

clue.text: Locum's back as I treat broken bones

indicators.note: the back of the word locum is its final letter
the letters of the words as I treat are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A stand-in doctor treats fractured bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' takes M from the end of 'Locum's'; 'broken' rearranges AS I TREAT as ETATARSI.
explanation.definitionFit: The five long bones of the foot between the ankle and toes.

clue.text: Work in the sea that was blue

indicators.note: the work goes inside the sea

parts.note: Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Working out at sea left someone feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel sad and listless is to have sulked around.

clue.text: Little boy knocking over cherry tree

parts.note: Al is a short form of boys' names such as Alan

indicators.note: the colour word is knocked over, read backwards

parts.note: cherry red is a bright colour

explanation.surface: A small boy knocks a cherry tree over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cherry tree' wants to be one item; 'cherry' is the colour red and 'tree' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A birch-family tree that grows in damp ground near rivers.

clue.text: Dental assistant's practice

definitions.meaning: the dentist's whirring tool that assists in work on teeth

explanation.walkthrough: 'assistant' suggests a nurse, but it is the dentist's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist's boring tool, and repeated training exercises.

clue.text: No more brilliant stuff written on page — one has no inclination

indicators.note: in an across clue the following letters are written on, after, the page

parts.note: late means dead, no longer alive
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A writer with no more brilliant ideas on the page has lost all enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no inclination' sounds like lack of desire, but means no slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A high area of level ground, flat with no slope.

clue.text: Glorious under tree

parts.note: sub is Latin for under
the lime is a tree, the linden

explanation.surface: It is wonderful underneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Supremely excellent or awe-inspiring.

clue.text: More romantic when newly married, inspiring love at last

indicators.note: breathing in, so holding the next letter inside
the word married is made anew, its letters rearranged
the final letter of the word love

explanation.surface: Newlyweds are more starry-eyed, love breathing into them at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges MARRIED as DRAMIER; 'inspiring' takes in E, the last letter of 'love'.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word meaning dreamy and sentimental, lost in fancy.

clue.text: Return of archer with record shot

indicators.note: the whole sequence is returned, read back to front

parts.note: William Tell, the Swiss archer who shot an apple off his son's head
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An archer comes back with a record-breaking shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns TELL and EP back to front together, giving PE + LLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round lead ball fired from an airgun.
